Also decide whether to neutralize `%%` comments and `#` tags in titles.

title: Restrict trail transitions to Chrome's known values
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`trail.transition` in delivered activity events is accepted as free text up to 64 characters (host/src/capture.rs ~136, activity shape check). Today it is stored only inside the hex marker payload, but the step 6.6 index reader will read it, so an unvalidated worker-supplied string becomes index input. title: (BUG) Process-group kill tests race under load
description: service::child::tests::killed_slot_yields_closed and service::command_runner::tests::kill_ends_the_whole_process_group fail intermittently on origin/main (5be16d3) under machine load: run alone 8 times each at load average 19-31 on 2026-11-02, they failed 4/8 and 1/8. In the child failure the kill reached `sleep 30` ("/bin/sh: line 1: <pid> Killed: 9 sleep 30") but the parent sh survived and printed "late"; in the runner failure the turn answered "started\n" instead of failing. Likely the shell has not yet joined or left its process group when ProcessSlot::kill signals it, or only the child was signalled. Fix the race in ProcessSlot/LineChild (or the tests' readiness handshake), without widening the time limits or weakening the assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests pass 50 consecutive isolated runs on macOS while the machine is under load (for example a concurrent cargo build), with no relaxed assertions or longer limits.
notes: Cookie 2026-11-02 queue review: acceptance explicitly requires 50 isolated runs under macOS load. This Linux VM cannot produce that evidence; left open without changing assertions or claiming certification.
close_reason: Root cause: on macOS a group SIGKILL can end the background sleep before it reaches the leader; the shell, woken from wait by that exit, ran on and exited 0 before its own SIGKILL took effect (a C probe outside Rust reproduced it: killpg left sh alive 22/50, kill(leader) first 0/50). ProcessSlot::kill now signals the leader directly, then the group. Under load (ambient ~30 plus 8 yes loops), 50 isolated runs each: killed_slot_yields_closed 36/50 -> 0/50 failures, kill_ends_the_whole_process_group 41/50 -> 0/50, new kill_ends_a_leader_waiting_on_its_child 50/50 -> 0/50; no assertions relaxed or limits widened; all README gates green.

(2) New request forget_adopted_contracts { expected_revision } (the state revision from (1)). Under the config lock the host rereads the file; if the revision still matches it renames it aside to adopted-contracts.json.<timestamp>.bak (the backup_invalid pattern for config.toml), then records the current contracts as a fresh file; a mismatch is conflict. Reply config_result. (3) Settings shows adopted_state.issue with a 'Forget recorded adapters' button explaining that notes from adapters removed by hand may need Use as artifact note again; the panel already shows the named refusal and may also show the issue. Update the refusal text (config::ADOPTED_CONTRACTS_REPAIR) to point at the button.

title: Refuse new strip_params entries that an adapter rule reads; warn and offer a one-click fix for existing ones

title: Service: keep a run's key until its terminal status is durable
description: Codex review of PR #75 (P2): Inner::finish in host/src/service/supervisor.rs frees the run's scheduler slot and key and drops its control even when the terminal write_status fails (disk full, permissions, transient I/O). Design choice needed: holding the slot until the write succeeds can strand the queue on a persistently failing disk, so prefer bounded retries plus an in-memory terminal state that get_run/list_runs report, keep the key reserved until the state is durable or the service restarts, and let recovery settle the record.
acceptance_criteria: A failing terminal status write never lets a second run start for the same record key, get_run reports the true end state, a later successful write or restart recovery makes the record durable, the queue is never stranded, fault-injection tests pin each case, and the full gate in the plan's Global Constraints is green.

close_reason: Shipped in the service-hardening PR: bounded terminal-write retries, in-memory end state, key kept reserved until durable.

title: Retain unsaved panel notes across close and reopen
description: Found while exercising brwr-9xg (related): the panel's pagehide flush queues behind an in-flight save and then immediately disconnects from the host, so the newest edits and any conflict copy-out exist only in memory and are lost when the panel closes. Add synchronous local recovery before save dispatch and explicit Copy/Discard after reopening, without silently applying a draft to a changed note. Cookie built this in cycle 8 (closed PR #67, commit 8ae533c on branch cookie/cookie-overnight/cycle-8-94fa9fc; never merged): a NoteRecovery store in extension/note-recovery.ts writes a snapshot to local storage in the input handler under a fresh immutable key per snapshot, so a save acknowledgement or a discard in another panel can only remove the exact snapshot it saw, never newer typing. Reopening shows the current note plus separate copy-out text (including conflicts and attempted empty deletions), and recovered text is never saved automatically. Reuse or rebase that work rather than redesigning it.

title: Replace the hand-written SQLite snapshot with an incremental real-SQLite index
description: Step 6.6 (host/src/index.rs) emits index.db with a custom SQLite file-format writer (build_sqlite) and keeps the real cache in index-state.json. Every publish re-derives all artifacts from the full event history, serializes the whole-history JSON state (64 MiB cap, after which index updates fail), and rewrites the entire index.db. Both are whole-file atomic replacements, so concurrent host processes are last-writer-wins. The writer supports no secondary indexes or overflow records, so M3 FTS5 cannot be built on it. Move to rusqlite with incremental upserts inside transactions (WAL, busy timeout), keep the daily log authoritative and brauser reindex as the full rebuild, and drop the hand-written writer and the whole-history JSON cache. Keep the existing 6.6 tests (hostile title, case-colliding ID, external edit replaced, heavy-use day with no file write, rollup bounds) passing.

title: Refuse an oversize start_run before contacting the service instead of reporting an unexpected reply
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 16); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. ServiceLink::request connects first (which can launch the LaunchAgent) and exchanges service_hello; only then does write_request refuse the body over the same cap (frame.rs:60-65). host/src/service/client.rs:243 wraps that as ServiceError::Protocol, and forward (native.rs:502-525) maps it to ErrorCode::Internal 'The Brauser service sent an unexpected reply.' Suggested fix: after resolving record_key, serialize once and, if over the cap, answer message_too_large (or invalid_request with a 'page is too large to send' message) before connecting. Same mechanism as review finding 0.

title: Reload the note under its new key when an external adapter change reaches the panel
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 5); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. scheduleReload (extension/panel.ts:491-511) runs reloadConfig and then `void notes.retry()` (panel.ts:507). NoteEditor.retry() (extension/note-editor.ts:140) calls showPage(this.target), which for the same URL only loads again when loadFailed is set (note-editor.ts:127-128). So when an adapter matching the open page is added or removed elsewhere (the settings page, or Capture Site in another window's panel), watchPolicy fires scheduleReload, the artifact card switches to 'Artifact recognized', but the editor keeps the stale URL key and revision. The user's next autosave sends expected_key kind url; host save_note answers note_conflict reason key_changed (host/src/native.rs:1510) and the typed text moves to the copy-out box. Repro (extension/tests/panel.test.mjs harness): load a URL-keyed note for https://github.com/acme/repo/pull/7, fire chrome.storage.onChanged with a lease of a new revision whose get_config returns an adapter matching that page, advance past the 250 ms reload, then type into the editor. Only one load_note is sent and the save carries expected_key.kind === 'url'. Suggested fix: have scheduleReload call notes.reload() (note-editor.ts reload) when the config revision changed, or whenever the editor is idle; keep the key_changed guard as the backstop. DESIGN.md §6.2 accepts key_changed for an edit already in flight; this is about the next edit after the panel was told.
acceptance_criteria: A panel test loads a URL-keyed note, delivers an external policy revision whose adapters now match the page, and asserts a second load_note is sent for that page before the next edit and that the following autosave sends expected_key.kind === 'artifact' with no note_conflict. A dirty draft in flight still gets the key_changed copy-out. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.

Full diff reviewed manually; no live-API Codex review permitted in this unattended workspace. Evidence: target/cookie-jdi-20261028/. macOS smoke refuses Linux.

title: Refresh the artifact card when any status refresh sees delivered_batches move
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 6); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. panelTick (extension/panel.ts:531-540) forces get_artifact only when the polled status's delivered_batches differs from session.status as it stood before the poll (deliveredSince at :539). pauseCapture (:548, refresh at :559), discardPendingVisits (:564, :581) and dismissNotices (:586, :596) also call session.refreshStatus(), which overwrites session.status (extension/settings.ts refreshStatus) without comparing delivered_batches. If a background delivery lands and the user clicks one of these before the next 30 s poll, the poll compares equal values and the card keeps stale focused time, days and last-seen until a tab change or the next delivery. Repro (panel.test.mjs): status delivered_batches=1 with rejected_count=1 so Dismiss is enabled; have the worker report delivered_batches=2; click dismiss-notices; fire the 30 s poll interval; no forced get_artifact is sent (a control without the click does send one). Suggested fix: do the delivered_batches comparison in one place (for example a wrapper around session.refreshStatus used by every caller, or keep a lastSeenDelivered counter that only refreshArtifact advances).
acceptance_criteria: A panel test raises delivered_batches, clicks Dismiss notices (and one of Pause or Discard), fires the poll, and asserts a forced get_artifact for the current page; the existing control (poll alone) still refreshes once, and an unchanged counter sends none. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.

title: Keep only the winning title's refs when the worker coalesces activity
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 29); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. coalesceActivity (extension/worker.ts:272) takes the newer title (merged.title = event.title ?? merged.title, worker.ts:285) but sets merged.refs to the union of old and new refs (worker.ts:295). extension/activity.ts:177-182 deliberately resets total.refs to the latest title's refs because the host re-derives refs from the current URL and title: check_activity_policy (host/src/native.rs:1072-1080) rejects any supplied ref not among them with 'activity_refs_mismatch'. So under queue pressure (80% of the item or byte cap), coalescing a same-artifact, same-hour duplicate whose newer title lacks the older title's ref yields an event the host rejects, losing that artifact-hour of activity. Repro (extension/tests/worker.test.mjs): fill the queue past the pressure threshold, queue an undispatched activity with title 'PROJ-1 fix' and refs [jira.issue PROJ-1], then freeze a same-artifact, same-hour total with title 'Release notes' and refs []; the coalesced item has title 'Release notes' and refs [PROJ-1]. Fix: take refs from whichever event supplies merged.title (deduplicated), matching activity.ts.
acceptance_criteria: A worker regression test coalesces two same-hour events with different titles under pressure and asserts merged.refs equals the refs of the event whose title won; when titles match, refs are still deduplicated and kept. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.
notes: Probe extension/tests/probe-coalesce-refs.test.mjs (rb-c2-v29). Pre-existing drift (2026-10-16); rare chain; low.
close_reason: Pressure-coalesced hourly activity keeps only the retained title event refs, deduplicated and bounded. Failing-first replacement plus three controls and full gate green (cycle commit; SHA assigned by driver).

title: Check retired adapter-ID history before Capture Site promises a save
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 28); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. siteConfigured (extension/capture-site.ts:31-33) and planCaptureSite (:35) read only config.adapters.artifacts; the ConfigSnapshot does not expose the retired contracts in [[adapter_id_history]] (host/src/config.rs:73, :1061, :1253). After a user removes a site whose hand-written adapter had a different id template or type than the starter (for example jira.issue on https://acme.atlassian.net with id 'jira:{host}/issues/{key}'), the panel offers Capture Site and the preview says 'Saving enables these pages.' (extension/capture-site-panel.ts:131), but update_config refuses the save in validate_adapter_transition_with_history (config.rs:2105, error at :1857 'the artifact type or id template ... cannot change until artifact migrations are available'), shown as 'Could not capture site: ...' (capture-site-panel.ts:215), and Capture Site stays on offer. Repro (config.rs tests): set that adapter, remove it so its contract moves to adapter_id_history, then ConfigStore::update with the exact document the Jira starter builds; it fails at commit. Suggested fix: expose the retired contracts (or a per-origin 'starter conflicts with retired contract' flag) in get_config and have planCaptureSite refuse up front with a message naming the retired adapter, or let the starter reuse the retired id template. The host refusal itself is intended policy (commit 1268180). brwr-hrc (merged as #85) is closed, which changes how retired contracts are recorded in config.rs; . config.rs and extension/settings.ts are also being edited by other lanes, so sequence after them.

title: Block Why saves on a site whose removal is still pending
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 20); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. whyPausedReason/whySaveBlocked (extension/panel.ts:289-310) check only config.capture_enabled === false and status.pause_pending; neither checks status.pending_removals. In that state the panel warns 'Some sites stay off until the settings page saves their removal in the host.' (panel.ts:448-449), and Capture Site already gates on pending_removals (extension/capture-site-panel.ts:107, :194). title: Re-check the notes folder before a queued or resumed run launches
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 13); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. run_cwd (host/src/service/server.rs:335-353) checks only config.configured() and stores the storage root as the run's cwd; it never calls Vault::open_checked against root_identity, which the native host's key resolution does. The cwd goes into Launch (host/src/service/supervisor.rs:390, :413) and status.cwd, and resume (supervisor.rs:335-347) takes it back unchanged after a service restart. Inner::run (supervisor.rs:663-669) re-reads agent.env when a run leaves the queue but uses launch.cwd as is (RunSpec at :761). VaultCheckFinisher::save (supervisor.rs:107-124) checks only the current config, so a run queued under folder A that starts after the user switched to folder B runs its harness in A and still ends Succeeded with the old start_key. Repro (supervisor.rs tests): seed_record a queued run with cwd = old-notes, switch config.toml to new-notes with a new root identity, start the service; the fake harness's pwd is old-notes and the run ends Succeeded. Latent in release builds (HarnessRegistry registers no runner); real once PR 3 adds one. Suggested fix (fail closed): when a run leaves the queue or resumes, re-resolve the notes folder under lock_current with Vault::open_checked and fail the run with not_configured/invalid_config if it no longer matches the recorded cwd. Same root cause as review finding 15 (record key, cwd and save resolved under different revisions), which the skeptic refuted on its own; this bead covers the queue/resume window only.
acceptance_criteria: A supervisor regression test queues (and separately resumes) a run recorded under one notes folder, switches the configured folder, and asserts the run fails with a not_configured or invalid_config error and the harness never starts in the old folder; a run whose folder is unchanged still launches there. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.
notes: Probe service::supervisor::tests::probe_resumed_run_uses_stale_cwd_after_notes_folder_change (rb-c2-v13). Skeptic marked it near-duplicate of finding 15; low and latent. Touches the service run path, which open access PR 3 (brwr-sr3, Magellen) is reworking; do not start until brwr-sr3 closes, then re-check the anchors against its result.
close_reason: Fixed in open access PR 3 (#98, feat/agent-runners-pr3) review fixes: a queued or resumed run re-checks its folder against the configured knowledge base folder and its recorded identity, under the config lock, when it starts, and fails closed before its harness.

title: Render sub-minute activity as <1 min instead of 0 min
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). measures() (host/src/index.rs:1875) formats focused and background time with whole_minutes() (index.rs:1802, seconds / 60), so 1-59 seconds renders "focused 0 min" or "0 min in background". It feeds the worklog text (Index::worklog, index.rs:793, lines ~855 and ~868) and the artifact Timeline rollups in render_artifact (index.rs:1728, ~1793). Fix: show "<1 min" when 0 < seconds < 60 in these rendered strings. Leave the numeric focused_min/background_min frontmatter fields (index.rs ~1747-1754) as integers. The panel already shows seconds (extension/panel.ts duration(), ~112) and needs no change. Update DESIGN.md §5.1/§5.7 wording if it states the rendering.

description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). loadRecent and loadWorklog (extension/panel.ts:605 and :632) return immediately while !session.connected, and the startup IIFE (panel.ts ~815-840: hello, reloadConfig, refreshActiveTab, replayVisits) never reloads them. title: Canonicalize event_id in captured payloads so rescans keep them
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). An activity or why event whose event_id is a valid UUID but not lowercase hyphenated (for example uppercase, or no hyphens) is accepted: CaptureStore::record_activity (host/src/capture.rs:244) returns CaptureOutcome::Persisted. record_entry (capture.rs:770, parse_event_id at :791, hashed at :910) and prepare_batch_entry (capture.rs:604, :622, :667) hash parse_event_id()'s canonical form (capture.rs:1398) into the marker's id_hash, but the hex payload is built from the raw event (record_activity payload clone ~:284, prepare_batch_activity :684-760, record_why :342-378 via serde_json::to_value(event)). On rescan, parse_marker_event (host/src/index.rs:1366) requires sha256(event.event_id) == id_hash (index.rs:1403 activity, :1422 why), so the line is silently dropped and the artifact disappears from the index. Repro: in host/src/index.rs tests, open a CaptureStore with CaptureStore::open_in(&storage(root), None, state) and policy enabled for https://example.com, build activity(...) with occurred_at = now (seconds precision) and event_id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string().to_uppercase(), assert record_activity returns Persisted, then Index::reindex() and assert index.artifact(&event.artifact_id) is Some. It is None on 1c32114. Suggested fix: write the canonical id into the payload at capture (for example insert "event_id" into the marker object next to where record_entry/prepare_batch_entry already insert the normalized "url", capture.rs:653 and :838), covering single activity, batch activity, and why. Optionally also recover lines already written with a raw id by comparing against the canonicalized payload id on rescan. Update 2026-10-27 (lane C2 seam review, findings 18 and 25, re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4): still reproduces, also for unhyphenated uppercase ids. record_summary already does the right thing: it canonicalizes with parse_event_id before building the marker (host/src/capture.rs:408-415, comment at :408-411) and its test a_noncanonical_uuid_summary_hashes_and_serializes_the_same_spelling (capture.rs:2849-2884) pins it. Copy that approach to the other writers, whose payload still keeps the raw spelling: record_activity (payload = event.clone() at capture.rs:296, serialized at :337), record_why (serde_json::to_value(event) at :373), and batch activity prepare_batch_activity (payload clone at :730, serialized at :764); record_entry (:782, parse_event_id at :803) and prepare_batch_entry (:616, :634) hash the canonical form. The index check is parse_marker_event (host/src/index.rs:1531) at :1568 (activity) and :1587 (why). Mirror the summary test with event_id = canonical.to_uppercase().replace('-', "") for activity and why, then reindex and assert the artifact keeps its focused_seconds and why.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test captures an activity event with an uppercase UUID event_id, asserts Persisted, reindexes, and asserts the artifact is present; a second case covers a why event (single or batch path); each case also uses the unhyphenated uppercase spelling, mirroring a_noncanonical_uuid_summary_hashes_and_serializes_the_same_spelling, and asserts the payload event_id equals the canonical form. Rescans keep lowercase-id events unchanged and still reject a payload whose id does not match the marker hash. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.
notes: Probe on local branch probe/lanec-idxw (probe_i5a_uppercase_event_id_survives_a_rescan). P3: real browsers send crypto.randomUUID() lowercase ids, so only a non-standard client hits it. Lane C2 probes: index::tests::probe_v18_noncanonical_event_id_survives_reindex (rb-c2-v18) and index::tests::probe_noncanonical_activity_and_why_ids_survive_reindex (rb-c2-v25); lowercase controls pass.
close_reason: Canonical activity/Why payload and live-index UUIDs preserve rebuilt work; batch replies echo request IDs. Test-first regressions and full gate green on base 46b46495; cycle commit pending driver. Historical recovery tracked by brwr-smu.

title: Bound captured URLs after normalization so rescans keep them
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). Capture checks the raw URL length (event.url.len() > MAX_URL_BYTES at host/src/capture.rs:627 and :802; mode and trail URLs in activity_shape_is_valid at capture.rs:154 and :166) but then stores normalize_url()'s output (capture.rs:1469; page URL inserted at :653/:838, mode URLs at :295/:727, trail from_url ~:313). Percent-encoding can triple the length, so a URL under 8192 bytes raw can be over 8192 normalized. The line is persisted, but on rescan parse_marker_event (host/src/index.rs:1366) applies safe_page_url (index.rs:1483, value.len() <= 8192) to the stored URL at :1396-1402 and drops the event. Repro: in host/src/index.rs tests, capture through CaptureStore::record_activity with event.url = format!("https://example.com/{}", "\u{fc}".repeat(3000)) (6 KB raw, about 18 KB encoded), modes cleared, occurred_at = now; assert Persisted, then Index::reindex() and assert index.artifact(&event.artifact_id) is Some. It is None on 1c32114. Fix: apply the 8192-byte bound after normalization for the page, mode, and trail URLs in every capture path (single, batch, why), rejecting with url_too_long, so nothing is acknowledged that the index will later refuse.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test shows a URL under 8192 bytes raw but over 8192 after normalization is rejected at capture with reason url_too_long (page URL, plus at least one mode or trail URL case), rather than persisted and later dropped; a URL whose normalized form fits is still persisted and survives reindex. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.
notes: Probe on local branch probe/lanec-idxw (probe_i5b_url_that_grows_past_8kib_when_normalized_survives_a_rescan).
close_reason: Reject normalized page/mode/trail URLs above 8192 bytes before vault writes; boundary URLs survive reindex. Test-first regressions and full gate green on base 46b46495; cycle commit pending driver.

title: Keep the older note's URL when migrating it to the artifact note
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). use_as_artifact_note (host/src/note.rs:586-636) renders the migrated note with render_note(artifact_key, destination_url, ...) at note.rs:622, so the artifact note records the route the migration was clicked from. save_keyed_note (note.rs:156, effective_canonical_url at ~216-227) keeps an artifact-keyed note's original URL instead. title: Preserve single-event recovery across presentation changes
description: Discovered while reviewing brwr-1fo: VisitIntent v1 stores only the hash of the rendered entry. After an upgrade changes escaping or Unicode filtering, a legacy single-event intent whose marker was not completed compares the new rendered bytes with the old hash and returns retryable/manual repair. Complete markers still deduplicate; compact batch intents retain their exact prepared bytes. This is fail-closed and preserves the log, but the queued legacy visit cannot finish automatically. Give single-event recovery a bounded representation independent of future renderer revisions, with an explicit safe recovery path for older intents; never guess at or overwrite an edited log.
acceptance_criteria: A regression starts with pre-upgrade legacy intent/hash and torn bytes, then retries under a changed renderer without losing the event, duplicating a complete marker, or changing unrelated log bytes. Altered logs, changed selected roots and mismatched payloads remain refused. Cover legacy records drained through both single and batch delivery. Keep any persisted prepared bytes bounded and host-owned.
notes: Completed v2 prepared-byte journals with 512 KiB entry/1 MiB serialized caps and frozen renderer-independent payload identity. V1 recovery retained explicitly. Four new regressions, 52 capture tests and full required/README gate green: 923 Rust outcomes including 43 explicit IPC skips, all 15 extension and two script files, 10,696 inert renderings. Complete diff reviewed locally; no live API or macOS smoke. Driver commit pending, based on ba8ee6b3; .bosun_commit_msg prepared.
close_reason: Retain bounded prepared bytes and normalized payload identity for single-event recovery through single and batch delivery; acceptance and full gate green. Cycle commit pending driver, based on ba8ee6b3; message in .bosun_commit_msg.
